title: Reconcile and recover the Genesis/DR seed from one bootstrap intent

in_scope: Read-only discovery and adoption of an existing provider substrate through an opaque adapter binding.
In-place reconciliation and recovery of the adopted protected Genesis substrate; future create-capable site classes use the generic BootstrapIntent contract, not this runbook.
Resolution of immutable node images across approved architectures through the image port.
Talos node configuration, Kubernetes bootstrap, Cilium networking, durable seed storage, and Genesis OpenBao establishment.
Enrollment of independent downstream cells through revocable identity and bounded mesh exports.
Verification, rollback, recovery, and quiescing of the Genesis authority.
out_of_scope: Tenant or application workload scheduling on the Genesis seed.
Routine fleet management, placement, CAPI controllers, continuous delivery, or customer serving traffic.
Shared Kubernetes membership, etcd, cluster authorities, credentials, or storage between seed and cells.
Public exposure of Kubernetes, Talos, OpenBao, provider metadata, or provider control endpoints.
Provider-native identifiers, shapes, network objects, or credentials in the provider-neutral intent.
protected_resources: The adopted Genesis seed compute and boot-storage binding must never be terminated by this runbook.
The external unseal key, recovery recipients, encrypted recovery artifacts, and audit records are separate protected lifecycles.
Existing independent cells must continue serving when Genesis or fleet-management authority is unavailable.

phases.success: The intent is schema-valid, capability-complete, provider-neutral, and contains only opaque binding and credential references.
phases.failure: Any invalid field, provider-native primitive, raw credential, ambiguous ownership, or unbounded cleanup target rejects the request.
phases.rollback: No mutation is allowed in this phase; return typed validation failures and preserve the prior accepted revision.

phases.success: Capability, jurisdiction, architecture, quota, failure-domain, and cost constraints resolve to one adapter binding revision.
phases.failure: No eligible binding, stale inventory, insufficient quota, or conflicting policy leaves the request blocked without fallback drift.
phases.rollback: Discard the unaccepted resolution proposal; do not mutate existing placement or weaken required capabilities.

phases.success: Exactly one existing protected substrate binding matches intent and carries explicit ownership and protection evidence.
phases.failure: Missing, duplicate, ambiguous, unmanaged, over-quota, create, replacement, termination, or retirement plans fail before provider mutation.
phases.rollback: Discard the adoption proposal and preserve the existing protected binding without mutation.

phases.success: A signed, content-addressed, architecture-compatible node-image release and provenance receipt are bound.
phases.failure: Missing architecture, signature, provenance, firmware, boot-mode, or adapter compatibility blocks node mutation.
phases.rollback: Retain the last-known-good image binding and quarantine the rejected candidate digest.

phases.success: The node OS is healthy on the desired immutable release with fresh trust and no secret-bearing provider metadata dependency.
phases.failure: Boot, trust, disk, time, private-management, or configuration validation failure stops before cluster bootstrap.
phases.rollback: Use the qualified node-image rollback slot or in-place recovery; never terminate the protected seed or restore compromised trust.

phases.success: The independent Kubernetes API and local etcd reach declared health with bootstrap performed exactly once.
phases.failure: Duplicate bootstrap, authority mismatch, unhealthy etcd, or API readiness failure blocks all higher phases.
phases.rollback: Preserve current node trust, collect redacted state, and recover from the last verified cluster receipt without joining another cluster.

phases.success: The selected datapath is sole CNI, policy enforcement and service routing pass, and provider metadata is denied by default.
phases.failure: Multiple CNIs, legacy proxy state, failed connectivity, metadata reachability, or public control exposure blocks progress.
phases.rollback: Restore the last qualified network revision or return to a fresh cluster state using the same trust revision.

phases.success: Dedicated retained data and audit volumes are Ready, correctly bounded, unbound before use, and covered by recovery policy.
phases.failure: Unexpected binding, wrong capacity, wrong node affinity, unsafe reclaim, or missing backup headroom blocks secret authority.
phases.rollback: Remove only uninitialized claims or newly created owned resources; preserve any initialized or incident-quarantined volume.

phases.success: Persistent OpenBao uses integrated Raft, TLS, external auto-unseal, independent custody, audited non-root administration, and verified restore.
phases.failure: Initialization ambiguity, excessive identity rights, seal failure, plaintext, missing custody, audit loss, or restore failure stops enrollment.
phases.rollback: Before initialization remove the workload and identity grant; after initialization isolate and preserve key, data, audit, and snapshots without wiping.

phases.success: Outside-in seed health, bounded local telemetry, immutable transition evidence, and recovery freshness signals are available.
phases.failure: Missing death detection, audit continuity, backup freshness, or bounded queue behavior prevents readiness claims.
phases.rollback: Keep the seed in provisioning-disabled state while established cluster and secret data remain isolated and recoverable.

phases.success: An independent cell receives short-lived identity and only explicitly approved routes and service exports.
phases.failure: Shared authority, overlapping addressing, broad routes, unbounded credentials, or failed revocation rejects attachment.
phases.rollback: Withdraw exports and routes first, revoke the attachment identity second, then remove trust material and prove reachability is absent.

phases.success: The independent cell meets its serving SLO through a declared Genesis outage while mutations fail closed and retries remain bounded.
phases.failure: Any serving dependency on Genesis, fail-open mutation, retry storm, replay, or recovery drift keeps provisioning frozen.
phases.rollback: Restore Genesis availability and the frozen attachment revision, preserve failure evidence, and do not authorize additional cells.

phases.success: Genesis retains only recovery, trust, health, and bounded enrollment readiness with no routine fleet or serving workload.
phases.failure: Unexpected controllers, tenant workloads, public exposure, or hot-path dependencies prevent quiescent status.
phases.rollback: Disable new provisioning, isolate the unexpected workload, and restore the last verified Genesis-only revision.

safety_rules.achieves: Prevents loss of the only approved Genesis substrate while recovery automation matures.
safety_rules.origin: The existing seed is explicitly protected and replacement or termination would expand blast radius and cost risk.
safety_rules.rule: The reconciler must reject termination, instance replacement, or unscoped full-disk reset of the adopted Genesis seed.
safety_rules.ensure: Adapter plan validation resolves the protected binding and denies destructive actions before provider execution.
safety_rules.overturn_when: A reviewed migration proves a separately healthy Genesis replacement, clean restore, static stability, and explicit authority to change the protected binding.

safety_rules.achieves: Keeps the same bootstrap intent portable across native, public-cloud, virtualized, and bare-metal substrates.
safety_rules.origin: Provider identifiers and products in canonical cell intent created lock-in and made migration a rewrite.
safety_rules.rule: The intent contains capabilities and policies only; provider names, identifiers, SKUs, regions, and network primitives exist solely in adapter bindings and adapter-owned receipts.
safety_rules.ensure: Schema validation and a semantic gate reject provider vocabulary outside registered adapter-owned paths.
safety_rules.overturn_when: A recorded challenge proves a specific value is a universal capability rather than a provider mechanism and updates the contract and gate together.

safety_rules.achieves: Prevents credentials and root material from entering Git, receipts, plans, logs, or controller state.
safety_rules.origin: Bootstrap configurations and provider metadata previously exposed full trust material to ordinary workloads.
safety_rules.rule: Bootstrap intent and receipts carry only scoped SecretProvider handles and digests; secret values are resolved at the execution boundary and never serialized into canonical state.
safety_rules.ensure: Admission, redaction, log, diff, and repository secret gates fail closed on credential-shaped material.
safety_rules.overturn_when: An approved cryptographic envelope provides equal non-disclosure, independent custody, rotation, and automated scanning guarantees.

safety_rules.achieves: Makes retries safe and prevents duplicate or conflicting resources.
safety_rules.origin: Imperative bootstrap sequences recreated resources because they trusted stale local state.
safety_rules.rule: Every phase begins with authenticated observation and compares desired, last-receipted, and current state before proposing mutation.
safety_rules.ensure: No adapter apply is callable without a fresh observation digest and a plan bound to the same revision.
safety_rules.overturn_when: A formally verified transactional substrate proves equivalent exactly-once behavior without pre-mutation observation.

safety_rules.achieves: Makes bootstrap resumable, reviewable, and recoverable after process or network loss.
safety_rules.origin: Chat and unstructured operator history did not survive sessions or prove the last completed transition.
safety_rules.rule: A successful transition is not complete until its immutable redacted receipt is durably written and read back.
safety_rules.ensure: The state machine cannot enter the next phase until receipt digest, ownership, and readback gates pass.
safety_rules.overturn_when: A stronger durable operation ledger provides equivalent immutable ordering, redaction, and independent recovery evidence.

safety_rules.achieves: Avoids circular recovery where the only keys or snapshots live inside the system they must recover.
safety_rules.origin: An auto-unseal service cannot recover from loss of its external seal mechanism using recovery shares alone.
safety_rules.rule: Recovery recipients, unseal-key administration, break-glass material, and encrypted snapshots have independently verified custody outside the seed.
safety_rules.ensure: Initialization and recovery stop until independent recipients and a clean-room readback or restore receipt exist.
safety_rules.overturn_when: A separately recoverable owned hardware root and quorum service demonstrably replaces the external custody boundary.

safety_rules.achieves: Bounds Genesis and fleet-management outages away from established serving cells.
safety_rules.origin: Hyperscaler cells must continue serving from local state when central control authority is impaired.
safety_rules.rule: Established cells never depend on Genesis for serving requests, cluster membership, local policy verification, runtime secrets, or data paths.
safety_rules.ensure: A declared outage test measures serving SLO, denies mutations, bounds retries, and detects all seed-address traffic.
safety_rules.overturn_when: A reviewed architecture demonstrates a smaller blast radius and equal availability without a central serving dependency.

safety_rules.achieves: Reduces exposure of the highest-authority APIs and metadata endpoints.
safety_rules.origin: Genesis APIs and provider identity carry disproportionate blast radius if exposed or reachable from ordinary workloads.
safety_rules.rule: Talos, Kubernetes, OpenBao, provider metadata, and bootstrap control endpoints remain private and are never published as public service names or ingress.
safety_rules.ensure: Outside-in probes must fail while approved private management and exact workload policy probes pass.
safety_rules.overturn_when: A separately accepted zero-trust public-control design proves phishing-resistant identity, device posture, workload isolation, rate limits, and equivalent failure containment.

prerequisites.required_evidence: A new authenticated state receipt whose freshness window covers the proposed operation.
An opaque adapter receipt proves exact ownership, protected-resource flags, cleanup scope, and current observed binding.
The latest encrypted recovery artifact passes size, digest, envelope, and independent readback verification.
A bounded private Talos and Kubernetes management path and an independent console recovery path are available.
Node OS, Kubernetes, network, and secret-authority artifacts resolve to exact digests with required signatures and provenance.
Current capacity, quota, storage headroom, and cost guard observations admit the plan without an uncontrolled spike.
Named independent recovery recipients, a separate bootstrap-administrator recipient, and an approved clean-room recovery procedure exist.
Exact workload admission, metadata isolation, key-use policy, crypto-service logging, TLS, audit export, and rollback boundaries pass before initialization.
A downstream cell has independent control-plane trust, non-overlapping addressing, local policy enforcement, and a revocable mesh intent.
The current operation, blast radius, maintenance window, and any human ceremony are explicitly authorized and recorded.

recovery_modes.when: The prior receipt is stale but no failed component or drift has been established.
allowed: Read provider, node, cluster, network, storage, identity, key, secret-authority, and recovery evidence.
Emit a new immutable state receipt.
forbidden: Any provider, node, cluster, identity, key, storage, or DNS mutation.
recovery_modes.success: A fresh receipt either proves the desired state or identifies the first incomplete or drifted transition.

recovery_modes.when: The protected substrate is reachable and failure is bounded to software, configuration, policy, or a recoverable boot slot.
allowed: Apply a hash-locked validated revision through private management.
Use a qualified rollback slot and scoped reset that preserves protected data.
forbidden: Terminate or replace the protected seed.
Restore superseded trust or perform an unscoped full-disk reset.
recovery_modes.success: The same protected binding returns healthy with desired trust, software, policy, storage, and recovery evidence.

recovery_modes.when: The substrate and clean software are healthy but cluster or secret-authority state is lost or corrupt.
allowed: Restore only an exact digest-verified artifact into an isolated target before promotion.
Use external custody and the approved unseal mechanism.
forbidden: Restore state into a mismatched software, trust, or adapter binding revision.
recovery_modes.success: Clean-room verification proves identity, integrity, health, audit continuity, and the expected nonsecret canary before service exposure.

recovery_modes.when: Software state is irrecoverable but the protected substrate, approved image, external trust, and recovery artifacts remain valid.
allowed: Reinstall the qualified immutable node image in place.
Recreate cluster software with fresh trust and restore only approved durable state.
forbidden: Delete the protected provider binding, boot storage, unseal key, or last verified recovery artifact.
Reuse compromised bootstrap trust or secret-bearing metadata.
recovery_modes.success: The same protected substrate is reconstructed and every phase from node OS through quiescence emits a new verified receipt chain.

verification.success: The binding digest, ownership, protection, quota, and cleanup scope match the approved plan.
verification.failure: Any identity, ownership, protection, quota, or cleanup drift is present.

verification.success: Node stage, services, disk, time, boot, and machine readiness all pass on the approved release.
verification.failure: Any required service, boot, storage, time, or readiness condition is degraded.

verification.success: API readiness, etcd leader and applied state, CoreDNS, and node conditions pass.
verification.failure: API, etcd, DNS, or node readiness is unhealthy or ambiguous.

verification.success: One CNI owns the datapath; service, DNS, policy, metadata isolation, and public-negative probes pass.
verification.failure: Legacy datapath state, failed connectivity, metadata reachability, or public control exposure is observed.

verification.source: Talos volume and Kubernetes persistent-volume state
verification.success: Data and audit volumes have exact capacity, secure mount, retention, ownership, and binding state.
verification.failure: Capacity, filesystem, mount, reclaim, affinity, ownership, or binding differs.

verification.source: OpenBao health, Raft, audit, and recovery receipts
verification.success: TLS, auto-unseal, single-voter Raft, non-root administration, audit, snapshot, restart, and isolated restore pass.
verification.failure: Any plaintext, seal, identity, custody, audit, snapshot, restart, or restore failure occurs.

verification.success: Ciphertext size and digest match, recipients are external, and clean-room extraction or restore succeeds.
verification.failure: Artifact missing, mismatched, circularly custodied, undecryptable, or unrestorable.

verification.success: A repeated request produces no mutation when desired and observed state already match.
verification.failure: A repeated request creates, rotates, initializes, bootstraps, or deletes anything unexpectedly.

verification.success: After injected interruption the operation resumes at the first incomplete phase without duplicate identity or resources.
verification.failure: The operation restarts completed phases, skips an incomplete phase, or loses ownership evidence.

verification.source: identity, route, and synthetic reachability receipts
verification.success: Only approved exports are reachable and detach plus revocation remove them within the declared bound.
verification.failure: Broad, transitive, residual, or unauthorized reachability remains.

verification.source: external synthetic serving and control observers
verification.success: The cell meets its serving SLO during Genesis outage with no serving request to Genesis.
verification.failure: Serving SLO fails, authorization fails open, retries storm, or any serving request depends on Genesis.

verification.source: cluster, network, identity, and workload inventory
verification.success: Only bounded recovery, trust, health, and enrollment readiness remain.
verification.failure: Routine fleet controllers, tenant workloads, public surfaces, or serving dependencies remain.

fault_injection.injection: Stop the reconciler after read-only adapter adoption resolves the protected binding but before its transition receipt is committed.
fault_injection.expected_behavior: The next run observes the same protected binding, emits the missing receipt, and performs no create, replacement, termination, or duplicate mutation.
fault_injection.recovery: Resume from the adoption transition using the same intent, observation digest, and operation ownership token.
fault_injection.safety_boundary: Qualify first against a synthetic adapter fixture; the protected seed path remains read-only throughout this injection.

fault_injection.injection: Change a canary binding after plan generation and before apply.
fault_injection.expected_behavior: The adapter rejects the stale plan before mutation and requires re-observation.
fault_injection.recovery: Generate a new observation and plan revision; never force the stale apply.
fault_injection.safety_boundary: Canary binding only; no protected resource mutation.

fault_injection.injection: Reboot a qualified non-production node during node or cluster convergence.
fault_injection.expected_behavior: Receipted phases are not repeated and reconciliation resumes only after node health returns.
fault_injection.recovery: Use the qualified boot rollback if health does not return; preserve operation and artifact evidence.
fault_injection.safety_boundary: Do not terminate or full-reset the protected seed.

fault_injection.injection: Deny the external unseal service during an isolated OpenBao restart test.
fault_injection.expected_behavior: OpenBao remains sealed, provisioning is disabled, audit records the failure, and no fallback credential is used.
fault_injection.recovery: Restore the exact unseal path and prove automatic unseal and expected key operations before resuming.
fault_injection.safety_boundary: Run first against scratch state; preserve production key and Raft data.

fault_injection.injection: Alter a disposable copy of the encrypted recovery artifact before clean-room restore.
fault_injection.expected_behavior: Digest or envelope validation fails before restore and the verified source remains untouched.
fault_injection.recovery: Discard the corrupt canary copy and re-read the immutable verified artifact.
fault_injection.safety_boundary: Never modify or overwrite the last verified recovery object.

fault_injection.injection: Stop the protected Genesis seed for the approved static-stability window without terminating it.
fault_injection.expected_behavior: Established cell serving continues within SLO; central mutations fail closed; retries remain bounded.
fault_injection.recovery: Start the same protected seed, verify exact binding and full health, then reconcile the frozen attachment once.
fault_injection.safety_boundary: Never terminate, replace, resize, detach storage, rotate trust, or change the approved binding during the trial.

success: A fresh receipt proves the protected Genesis substrate and every required software, network, storage, identity, recovery, and quiescence condition.
One provider-neutral bootstrap request can plan and reconcile this protected adopt-only target, then resume, verify, rollback, and quiesce through registered ports.
Exact rerun and injected-interruption tests prove idempotency, ownership-safe cleanup, and first-incomplete-phase resume.
Persistent OpenBao passes external auto-unseal, TLS, custody, audit, restart, encrypted snapshot, and clean-room restore gates.
An independent development cell attaches through revocable identity and meets its serving SLO during the declared Genesis outage.
Every transition receipt is redacted, immutable, content-addressed, remotely read back, and independently reviewed.
failure: Any plan can terminate or replace the protected seed, mutate an unowned resource, or expose a control endpoint publicly.
Any provider primitive or secret value leaks into provider-neutral intent, Git, Beads, receipts, logs, or controller state.
A rerun duplicates resources, trust, bootstrap, initialization, routes, or mutations, or cannot resume after interruption.
Recovery depends on the failed seed, lacks external custody, mismatches a digest, or cannot complete in a clean room.
An established cell loses serving availability, fails authorization open, or creates a hot-path dependency on Genesis.
nonclaims: This source-authored runbook does not implement or authorize the Rust reconciler.
This runbook does not establish current seed health, OpenBao readiness, mesh readiness, high availability, or production certification.
This runbook does not make the Genesis seed a routine fleet-management or serving plane.
This runbook does not qualify riscv64 or any unsupported architecture; architecture admission remains a release-profile decision.

failure_modes.detection: A receipt has expired or an observed binding digest no longer matches the plan.
failure_modes.containment: Block all mutation and retain the prior accepted intent and receipt chain.
failure_modes.recovery: Re-observe through authenticated read-only ports and produce a new plan bound to the fresh receipt.

failure_modes.detection: An adapter cannot prove whether a resource is adopted, protected, operation-owned, or unrelated.
failure_modes.containment: Reject apply and cleanup; do not infer ownership from names or location.
failure_modes.recovery: Establish an explicit adapter binding receipt or obtain human adjudication without mutating the resource.

failure_modes.detection: A phase proposes an effect already present in observed state or a prior accepted receipt.
failure_modes.containment: Reject the duplicate effect and freeze the operation ledger.
failure_modes.recovery: Reconcile receipts against current state, repair the missing receipt if evidence is sufficient, and resume at the first truly incomplete phase.

failure_modes.detection: A secret value, private key, token, certificate key, recovery share, signed URL, or secret-bearing configuration appears outside its approved provider.
failure_modes.containment: Stop output, revoke or rotate affected trust, quarantine artifacts, and prevent publication.
failure_modes.recovery: Regenerate trust from approved custody, rerun secret scans, and resume only from a clean receipt revision.

failure_modes.detection: OpenBao cannot auto-unseal, has no Raft leader, fails canary readback, or cannot restore the latest snapshot.
failure_modes.containment: Disable provisioning and isolate the service while preserving key, data, audit, and snapshot evidence.
failure_modes.recovery: Restore the external unseal path or perform the independently approved clean-room restore; never reinitialize over retained data.

failure_modes.detection: A serving request, runtime secret, local policy decision, cluster control path, or data path calls Genesis during the outage trial.
failure_modes.containment: Fail the gate, restore Genesis, freeze new enrollment, and preserve correlated traces.
failure_modes.recovery: Move the dependency into cell-local state with bounded validity, then repeat detach and full outage tests.

failure_modes.detection: A public DNS record, route, listener, or probe reaches Talos, Kubernetes, OpenBao, metadata, or bootstrap control surfaces.
failure_modes.containment: Withdraw the route or record, revoke exposed credentials, and block provisioning.
failure_modes.recovery: Restore private access with explicit policy, repeat outside-in negative probes, and rotate any potentially exposed trust.

failure_modes.detection: Rollback cleanup proposes deletion, replacement, termination, or data destruction for an adopted, protected, shared, or unreceipted resource.
failure_modes.containment: Reject cleanup before mutation and preserve all current resources.
failure_modes.recovery: Narrow cleanup to current-operation-owned resources; use quiescence for the protected seed, then re-plan with independent review.
